enchantment.hardcore_region_difficulty.a: Significantly increases armor protection beyond normal limits.
Deals massive additional damage to enemies.
Sets enemies ablaze for extended duration.
Reflects heavy damage back to attackers.
Greatly increases loot drops from mobs.
Dramatically increases mining and digging speed.
Knocks enemies back with tremendous force.
hardcore_region_difficulty.quality.disab: The quality system is turned off in the config.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.title: Hardcore Region Difficulty
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.show_r: Shows the region name and difficulty when you enter a new region. Default: on.

Traveler's Titles is installed: its title is shown and the difficulty is always displayed under it. This switch is locked. To hide titles, turn off "Enable Biome Titles" in the Traveler's Titles config.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.show_b: Shows a title when a boss or mini boss is nearby. Default: on.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.qualit: Off: no new qualities, no quality effects, no tooltip, Quality Forge locked. Items keep their quality, so turning it on again restores it. Default: on.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.high_t: How much faster the chance of HIGH qualities (Superior and above) grows with the level than the normal bonus per level. 1 = same as the normal bonus, 1.5 = default. Only for loot, mobs, inventory and villagers; the Quality Forge ignores weights and levels.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.unlock: On: HIGH qualities with chance 0 start to appear in regions from their "Unlock level" (see the Quality tab). Off: they never appear in regions. Does not affect the Quality Forge (it can always roll them).
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.low_qu: Low quality cut at top level (%)

How much the chance of low qualities is cut in the most dangerous regions. It grows with the level and reaches this value at the highest level of the mod, including levels you add (6, 7...). 0 = off. Levels with their own quality_bonus_percent ignore it.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.roll_i: Roll quality for items in inventory
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.qualit: Saved in hardcore_region_difficulty-quality.toml. In multiplayer the server's value decides the effects, so keep the client the same.
Edit the qualities below, or edit config/hardcore_region_difficulty-qualities.json by hand and run /hrd quality reload.
Each quality has a tier between the lowest and highest tier below. Tiers sort the qualities and set their default chance group; tier 0 is the standard quality.
0 or below (default -5). Qualities with a lower tier are raised to it. Save and reopen this screen to edit tiers beyond the old limit.
0 or above (default 5). Qualities with a higher tier are lowered to it. Save and reopen this screen to edit tiers beyond the old limit.
On: percent effects are clamped to -20%..+20% reach to -0.5..+0.5 and armor bonus to -0.5..+1.5. Off: only a safety range applies.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.region: You are connected to a server: its config file decides. Edit the regions from the main menu or on the server.

Pick from the list or type a texture (mypack:textures/gui/icon.png). Own images: put square .png files (lowercase names) in config/hardcore_region_config/icon/iconlevel and reopen. Empty = skull of the level.
Unknown icon: use a built-in name or namespace:path.png
Color of the difficulty title: a color name (gold, red...) or #RRGGBB. Empty = default.
Unknown color: use a color name or #RRGGBB
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.level_: Default title, icon and color of every region of a level. Levels 1-5 are region levels; 99 (mini boss) and 100 (boss) set the boss warning title and cannot be used by regions. For your own region level, fill '+ New level', tick 'Add this level' and use a number from 6 to 98.
Tick to create this level on save.
6 to 98 (99 and 100 are the boss levels, so it cannot go higher). Mobs scale by the 'per level' percents of this number, so a higher level is stronger.
Removes the definition (levels 1-7 go back to the default title and icon).
Default difficulty title of the regions of this level. Empty = 'Difficulty N'.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.whitel: Choose which mobs the difficulty scaling applies to and fine-tune each one. An empty list means no restriction (every eligible mob is scaled). Once a list has entries, only the matching mobs are scaled. A mob must pass the global list AND the list of the region it is in. Mobs on 'exclude_entities' of the file are never scaled. Raid mobs only follow the global list. To add a mob: open '+ New mob', type its ID and fill only the details you want to change, then save and reopen this screen. A '*' after a mob means it has custom details.
+ New mob %s
Not a number (leave empty for automatic)
Use a whole number from 1 up (or leave empty)
Mob
Which mob(s) this entry is about. Type an ID such as minecraft:zombie, a tag, a regex or * (see the syntax below).
Delete this mob
Remove this entry on save (the mob is no longer on the whitelist; if the list becomes empty, every mob is allowed again).
Details of this mob - leave a field empty to use the normal value of its level. A value you type replaces the level's value for this mob only.
Empty = automatic (formula or custom stats of the level).
Difficulty level
Treat this mob as if it stood in a region of this level (1 = no bonus), wherever it is.
Health bonus (%)
Total health bonus of this mob in %: 100 = double health, 0 = unchanged, minimum -90.
Damage bonus (%)
Total damage bonus of this mob in %: 100 = double damage.
Armor bonus (%)
Total armor bonus of this mob in %.
Flat armor (+points)
Armor points added to this mob.
Speed bonus (%)
Total movement speed bonus of this mob in %.
Knockback resistance (+0 to 1)
Added to the knockback resistance: 1 = the mob takes no knockback.
Follow range bonus (%)
How much farther the mob notices and chases targets, in %.
One entry per line: minecraft:zombie (exact id), #minecraft:skeletons (tag), ~^minecraft:.*spider$ (regex), * (all), !minecraft:creeper (everything except it).
Global whitelist (all regions)
Mobs
Only these mobs are scaled, in every region. Empty = all.
Whitelist per region
Open a region to give it its own whitelist. The number in brackets is how many entries it has.
Mobs
In this region only these mobs are scaled. Empty = all (still limited by the global list).
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.level_: Extra bonus of this boss class. It is added on top of the bonus of the level of the region where the boss is.
Extra bonus in % added to the normal bonus of the region level (e.g. 50 = +50% of the boss's base value).

Extra multiplier on the whole bonus of this boss class, applied after the % bonus above (1.0 = unchanged, 1.25 = 25% stronger). Separate per class: Boss and Mini-Boss do not share it. From 0.1 to 100.
Off: follows the formula. On: uses the values below.
Total bonus of this level (not per step). Health/Damage/Armor/Speed in %: 100 = double the mob's base value, 0 = unchanged, minimum -90. Flat armor in armor points.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.scalin: How much stronger mobs get with each level, for every level that has no custom stats. Level 1 is the base (no bonus); level N applies N-1 steps.
Off (default): each level multiplies on the previous one (compound). On: every step adds the same amount (e.g. 25% per level -> level 3 = +50%).
Bonus of ONE step (one level), in %. Armor flat: armor points per step.
From a certain level, mobs have a chance to become Elite: 1-2 random powers (fire, lightning, poison, regeneration, armored, swift, tough, vampiric), a colored name and particles. Bosses are never Elite.
Off: no new mob becomes Elite (existing Elites keep their powers). Default: on.

Follow global: uses the global "Enable elite mobs" switch. On / Off: forces elite spawn in this region, whatever the global switch says. Saved as "elite_enabled" of the region. Existing Elites keep their powers.

Follow global: uses the global "Enable elite mobs" switch. On / Off: forces elite spawn in this structure or dimension. Saved in the scan_ region of this entry (its level is kept as shown), without custom mob stats if those are off.
Only mobs of this level or higher can be Elite. Default: 4.
Chance (0 - 1) at exactly the minimum level, e.g. 0.15 = 15%. Default: 0.15.
Every level above the minimum adds this chance (0.08 = +8%). Chance = base + (level - minimum level) x this value, at most 1. Default: 0.08.
The minimum level and the next one give 1 affix, then +1 affix every 2 levels (2 from level 6 with the defaults), never above this number. Default: 2.

Each difficulty level can have at most this many living Elites at the same time. When an Elite dies or disappears (despawn, unload), another mob of that level can become Elite. 0 = no limit. Default: 1.
Shows a few particles around Elite mobs, one kind per affix.
Shows the affix list after the name, e.g. "[Elite] Zombie (Fire, Swift)". Off: only "[Elite] Zombie". Only applies to newly spawned mobs.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.scalin: Soft cap (level where it slows down)

From this level on, the % bonus per level grows more slowly (diminishing returns). Effective level = min(level, soft cap) + (level - soft cap) x factor. Example: soft cap 5, factor 0.75: level 9 counts as level 8. 0 = off. Default: 5. Levels with custom stats are not affected.
Every level above the soft cap only counts as this part of a normal level (0 - 1). 1.0 = no reduction, 0.75 = 75%, 0 = stops completely at the soft cap. Default: 0.75.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.qualit: Open a quality to edit it. Tick 'Delete' to remove one, or fill '+ New quality' to add one. Saving rewrites config/hardcore_region_difficulty-qualities.json and reloads it (main menu / single player only).
You are connected to a server: its quality file decides. Edit the qualities from the main menu or on the server.
Removes it from the file on save. Items that have it get a new quality.
Letters A-Z, digits and _ only. Leave empty to add nothing.
This ID already exists in this category
Empty = default name from the language file (or the ID).
Type a hex code like #FF8800 or use the picker.

-5..5. Used for sorting and as the default for the chance group. The Quality Forge and crafted items use ONLY the tier: its share (see the forge / crafted chances) is split equally between all qualities of the same tier, so your own qualities are balanced automatically. Several qualities at tier 0 share the standard chance.

Chance of this quality to be rolled, in % of its category, at difficulty level 1 (loot, mobs, inventory). NOT used by the Quality Forge and crafted items: they use fixed chances by tier (standard highest, bad ones likelier than good ones). The chances of one category do not have to add up to 100: they are scaled to 100 when rolling. 0 = never rolled (unless unlocked below). In dangerous regions the low qualities get rarer and the high ones more common on their own.
NEGATIVE: rarer in dangerous regions. NEUTRAL: unchanged. POSITIVE: more common. HIGH: more common, scaled by the high tier bonus.

Only used by HIGH qualities whose chance weight is 0 (e.g. Mythic, Divine).

A weight of 0 means the quality is never rolled normally. With a level here (and "unlock_high_qualities" on in the quality config) it starts to appear in regions whose difficulty level is this number or higher: it begins with weight 1 at that level and gains +1 every 2 levels above it (stretched when you add levels above 5, so it keeps its place on the scale).

Example: unlock 4 -> level 3 never, level 4 weight 1, level 5 weight 1, level 6 weight 2.
0 = never appears this way. Qualities with a weight above 0 ignore this field. Works for levels you added (6+) too.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.diffic: Off = the whole difficulty evaluation is disabled: no mob scaling, no titles, no difficulty based loot or quality bonus. Default: on.
WARNING: turning this off can affect existing worlds. Mobs that were already scaled keep their boosted stats, chests already opened keep their loot, and mobs spawned while it is off stay unscaled.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.qualit: WARNING: turning the quality system off can affect existing worlds. Items keep their quality tag but it stops working (no bonuses or penalties, no tooltip), and the Quality Forge is locked until you turn it back on.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.compat: Saved in hardcore_region_difficulty.json (mod_compat_settings). The game or server that loads the world reads it, so on a dedicated server edit the server's file.
On = Cataclysm gear is upgraded from Deeper and Darker Warden gear instead of netherite gear. Needs both mods installed. Applies after re-entering the world or /reload. Default: off.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.analyz: On = many hostile mobs around also raise the level. The radius and the thresholds show below while this is on. The level is held for 30 s so it does not flicker. Saved in hardcore_region_difficulty.json; on a dedicated server edit the server's file. Default: off.
WARNING: counting the mobs around is the most expensive part of Smart Auto and adds lag, more with a bigger radius or many mobs. Leave it off on weak servers.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.enemy_: Hostile mobs within this many blocks are counted (1-128). Default: 32. A bigger radius counts more mobs and costs more lag.

The level is reached when at least this many hostile mobs are within the radius. 0 removes this level from the table. Levels above the last one continue by themselves (auto_extend_thresholds in the file).
Type the number of a level (2 or more) to put it in the table, together with the minimum mobs below, then save. 0 = add nothing. Typing a level that is already there changes its minimum mobs.
Use 0 (nothing) or a level of 2 or more.
Add a level: minimum hostile mobs
Hostile mobs needed for the level typed above. It only counts when that level is 2 or more and this is at least 1.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.compat: Deeper and Darker and Cataclysm must both be installed to turn this on.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.enchan: WARNING: the enchantments of this mod can unbalance the game, so you may turn them off. But turning them off can affect existing worlds: items that already have the enchantment keep it but it has no effect, it stops appearing in loot, books and villager trades, and it can no longer be applied at an anvil. Loot that was already generated is not changed. Turning it back on restores everything.
Enable all enchantments of this mod
Off = every enchantment of this mod is off, whatever the individual switches below say. Default: on.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.boss.n: Health and damage of the vanilla bosses (saved in hardcore_region_difficulty-common.toml, applied when the boss loads; only works while the difficulty system is on). Health 0 means vanilla health.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.boss.h: Effective health of the boss. Minecraft caps max health at 1024, so a value above 1024 keeps max health 1024 and divides the damage the boss takes (2048 = it takes half damage). 0 = vanilla (Ender Dragon 200, Wither 300, Warden 500).
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.boss.d: Multiplies the damage the boss deals (before armor). 1.0 = vanilla.
hardcore_region_difficulty.regionshow.ti: Where you stand (click an id to copy it):
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.scalin: Type just the number. Every raid mob (including mobs of other mods) uses this fixed difficulty level instead of the level of the region. Allowed: 0 = off (use the level of the region the raid happens in), 1-5, and every level that exists in your config, including the ones you added (6+). Default: 3. A level you just created is accepted after you save and reopen this screen.
This level does not exist. Allowed numbers: %s
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.preset: Pick a built-in set of stats or one of your own presets: the per-level growth (health, damage, armor, speed), the extra bonus of mini bosses and bosses, the health / damage of the Ender Dragon, Wither and Warden, and the Raid difficulty level (Easy 2, Normal 3, Hardcore 4). When you change the preset and save, these values are overwritten (your own levels and whitelists are not changed). 'Custom' is shown when your values match no preset; choosing it changes nothing.
Pick a preset from the list.

Saves the stats you have set now (including what you just edited on this screen) as a new preset. Type a name and save: the preset shows up in the list after you reopen the screen. Stored in config/hardcore_region_difficulty-presets.json. The same name replaces the old preset.
Empty = do not create. Do not use the names Easy / Normal / Hardcore / Custom. With a name, this save only creates the preset and does not apply the preset chosen above.
Turn on and save to delete the own preset selected in the box above. Built-in presets cannot be deleted. The values in use do not change.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.level_: Off: quality chances follow difficulty_quality_bonus (higher level = better quality). On: uses the two values below for loot, villagers and inventory rolls made in regions of this level.
Total bonus of this level (not per step). 100 = good qualities twice as likely and bad ones half as likely, 0 = unchanged, negative = worse items (minimum -90).
Same for the high qualities (Superior and above). 300 = four times as likely, -90 = almost never.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.levelc: A region can only be as strong as its dimension allows: dimension level + bonus, and never above the highest level of the mod (5 by default, 6 when you create level 6, and so on).
Off: regions keep their own level in every dimension, no cap at all.
Cap = level of the dimension + this value. Default 2 (The End is level 3, so its cap is 5). Set it to 0 to keep a dimension at its own level.
0 = the highest level you created in the Levels list (5 if none). A number above 0 fixes the highest level of the mod.
Exact cap of one dimension, replacing dimension level + bonus. One entry per line as dimension=level, for example minecraft:the_end=4 or minecraft:the_nether=3. Wildcards like mod:* work.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.scan.n: Dimensions and structures found by the last scan (it runs when a world starts, or with /hrd scan). Change the level of one, and turn on custom stats to set the mob health, damage, armor and speed bonus there. Structures the scan ignores as safe are not listed; rate them in smart_auto_settings.structure_levels.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.scan.m: No scan file yet. Open a world once (or run /hrd scan), then come back here.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.scan.l: Difficulty level of this structure. 0 = ignored (no level from it). The default is what the scan found.
Minimum level of the whole dimension. 0 = no automatic level. It is also the base of the level cap of that dimension.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.scan.c: Off: mobs follow the formula of the level. On: every scaled mob in this structure or dimension gets the values below. Saved as a region named scan_...
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.scan.s: Total bonus here (not per step). 100 = double the mob's base value, 0 = unchanged, minimum -90.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.scan.r: Turn on and save to remove your level and mob stats for this entry: the level goes back to what the scan finds by itself and the stats follow the formula again. The scan_ region of this entry is deleted. A manual region of yours is not touched.
The whole setup is in the file HrdSetting.json of the config folder (the mod writes it if it is missing; /hrd export rewrites it from the current setup). To use another setup, put its file in the config folder, type its name below and save, or run /hrd import file.
Name of a setup file in the config folder, for example HrdSetting.json or myserver.json. Saved when you press Save.
An import replaces your whole config. The old files are saved as .bak-DATE in the config folder.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.loot.n: The higher the level, the more and better loot. All values are percent per level above 1, so level 1 is unchanged. Item quality chances per level are set in each level (Custom item quality chances).
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.loot.e: Off: no extra loot at all (the quality and enchant rules of the mod stay).
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.loot.m: Regions below this level get no bonus.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.loot.r: Chance, per level above 1, that the chest's loot table is rolled one more time. Level 4 with 10 = 30% per extra roll.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.loot.m: How many extra rolls a chest can get at most.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.loot.c: Stackable items (arrows, ingots, food) come in bigger stacks. At most x10.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.loot.e: Chance that unenchanted gear is enchanted, stronger in higher levels.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.loot.m: Mob extra drop chance per level (%)
Chance that a mob drops one more copy of an item it dropped. Gear copies get a new quality.
Mob stack size bonus per level (%)
Mob gear enchant chance per level (%)
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.tier_s: Share of the standard quality in the Quality Forge and crafted items. Only the ratio between the 5 numbers matters. Default 13 (about 26% with the other defaults).
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.tier_b: Share of all qualities that lower stats at tier -1, split equally between them. Default 14.
Each further negative tier gets this fraction of the previous one (0.5 = half). Default 0.5.
hardcore_region_difficulty.config.tier_g: Share of all tier 1 qualities that raise stats, split equally between them. Default 9.
Each further positive tier gets this fraction of the previous one. Mythic, Divine and Flawless are in the highest tiers. Default 0.4.
